fact.thing: 2026 tax refund on an $8,000 FHSA deposit for an Ontario resident earning about $60,000 to $80,000
fact.claim: FHSA contributions count for the calendar year from January 1 to December 31. Unlike RRSP contributions, money you put in during the first 60 days of 2027 can't be deducted on your 2026 return. In Ontario, taxable income between $58,523 and $107,785 is taxed at a combined federal and provincial rate of 29.65% in 2026 (20.5% + 9.15%), so deducting $8,000 cuts 2026 tax by about $2,372, before the Ontario surtax and credits, which can change the result at higher incomes. If you miss the deadline you don't lose the money: unused room and undeducted contributions carry forward, so the refund comes a year later. Participation room only starts in the year you open your first FHSA.

plain.what: An FHSA is a savings account for your first home, and money you put in lowers your tax bill. The FHSA only counts money that lands between January 1 and December 31. An RRSP, which is a retirement savings account, gives you 60 extra days into the new year. The FHSA does not.
plain.so_what: If you put $8,000 in and your Ontario income is between $58,523 and $107,785, that deposit cuts your 2026 tax by about $2,372, and a deposit that lands in January waits a whole year for it.
plain.do: Check the date your FHSA deposit actually lands and write it down.
